newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq defuses 3,800 allied bombs in two months.
newsitem.headline: Iraq defuses 3,800 allied bombs in two months.

text.p: Iraqi newspapers said on Thursday civil defence teams in the past two months found and defused more than 3,800 bombs the United States and its allies had dropped on Iraq during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.

"The total number of bombs, rockets and other ammunitions... found and treated throughout Iraq from February 1 to March 31 was 3,863," the papers said in identical reports on message they said Iraq's U.N. representative Nizar Hamdoun had delivered to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday.
The papers said the devices were of different kinds and sizes, including cluster shells.
In February Iraq announced that it had defused more than 352,000 bombs since the end of the Gulf War.

A number of people, including women and children, have been killed as a result of the explosion of bombs the allies dropped during their massive air campaign to force Iraq to withdraw its troops from Kuwait which it occupied in 1990.
